question.text: Mr. Aryan Gupta, IM of Panchamukhi Special Situations Fund (Cat II), is drafting the IC composition. An Accredited Investor LP demands a seat. Best-practice GP approach is:

answer.text: Grant OBSERVER seat with documented conflict-of-interest protocol and information-sharing NDA
Grant voting seat equal to the Manager's
Grant veto power over all investments

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Ch 9.4.1 Point 3, large ticket and Accredited Investors have representation rights. Best-practice: observer seat (no voting) with COI protocol — balances LP monitoring with GP autonomy. Voting/veto creates conflicts and delays IC decisions. The Trap: Option A violates SEBI rights. Options C and D overshoot and compromise IM fiduciary duty. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C (Compliance) on COI; XIX-C for IC drafting. Manager's Pro-Tip: Never let more than 2 observer seats onto an IC — the signal value (LPs feel heard) is preserved but meeting dynamics stay efficient. Minutes should be redacted for confidential deal terms before circulation to observers.
